definitions.explanation: Paint that is mixed with water rather than oil, producing translucent colors. Standard art material in Japanese schools.

examples.japanese: {水彩絵具|すいさいえのぐ}で{風景画|ふうけいが}を{描|えが}く。
examples.english: To paint a landscape with watercolors.

examples.japanese: {小学校|しょうがっこう}の{図工|ずこう}の{時間|じかん}に{水彩絵具|すいさいえのぐ}を{使|つか}った。
examples.english: We used watercolors in art class at elementary school.

examples.japanese: {水彩絵具|すいさいえのぐ}は{水|みず}で{薄|うす}めることで{淡|あわ}い{色合|いろあ}いを{出|だ}すことができる。
examples.english: By diluting watercolor paint with water, you can produce pale, delicate tones.

notes:
A compound of {水彩|すいさい} (watercolor) and {絵具|えのぐ} (paint). Watercolor painting is a standard part of the Japanese school curriculum, and nearly all elementary school students own a {水彩絵具|すいさいえのぐ}セット (watercolor paint set).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水彩絵具|すいさいえのぐ}セット: watercolor paint set
- {透明|とうめい}{水彩絵具|すいさいえのぐ}: transparent watercolors
- {不透明|ふとうめい}{水彩絵具|すいさいえのぐ}: opaque watercolors (gouache)
- {水彩絵具|すいさいえのぐ}を{溶|と}く: to mix watercolor paint (with water)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {油絵具|あぶらえのぐ}: oil paint — thicker, opaque, and takes longer to dry
- {絵|え}の{具|ぐ}: paint (general term) — covers all types of paint for art
- {水彩画|すいさいが}: watercolor painting — the finished work or the art form itself
